expectations.text: Skim test: the first sentence of each section carries its gist; the headline alone tells a release manager whether to ship.
expectations.evidence: Headline: '38/48 PASS, 9 FAILURE, 1 BLOCKED — not ready to merge.' followed by 'Three of the PR's four promised changes contradict the product specs'. Section openers carry the gist: each Non-PASS heading states the finding ('C02 — `list` dropped the priority column'), Issues opens with 'Critical — closed tickets can be reassigned and thereby reopened', UX gaps with 'Subcommand help is bare', Improvements with 'Reconcile PR and specs before merge', Leftover artifacts with 'All under OUTPUT_DIR, kept to reproduce the findings'.

notes: The run found all four planted changes by execution and held the specs over PR.md, so the substantive assertions discriminate well and were earned. Two gaps in the assertions: (1) 'the report shows the command' passed on shorthand like `close 2 "duplicate"` with the invocation prefix stated once; check_run's cli_commands_in_report=4 and transcript_cli_runs=5 undercount because the executor used a shell helper, so a wrong run that wrote shorthand with invented output would pass the same way. Consider requiring the observed output to match a live re-run of the stated command. (2) The transcript is executor-authored prose, not a tool log, so 'case list written before execution' rests on the executor's own ordering; the scratchpad file happened to exist here, but the assertion should name a file path the grader can stat. Also, the run read the diff (step 8) before deriving cases, which no assertion addresses; the skill may permit it for blast radius, but if 'black-box' matters, say so. The prose-lint assertion is the only one the old skill failed structurally (53 findings, mostly semicolons), and the one-missing-cause failure on E07 is a near miss worth noting when comparing skill versions.
